evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/util/FormatUtils.kt:18-24 — FormatUtils.formatPrice(price: Long, currency) documents '@param price The price in minor units (e.g., cents)', but the actual system contract is whole-currency units, so the docstring directly contradicts every real caller and the wire format.

The wire deserializer is explicit that prices are whole units: api/DecimalStringSerializers.kt:37-49 DecimalAsLongSerializer does `raw.substringBefore('.').toLong()` and its own doc says 'Prices in the portal models are whole-currency Longs, so the sub-unit scale carried by DECIMAL(15,2) is dropped' ('200000.00' -> 200000). listing/ListingModels.kt:96,123 declare `val price: Long` fed by that serializer.

All 10 production call sites pass the whole-unit `listing.price` (e.g. androidApp .../ui/listing/ListingHeaderSection.kt:55, ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:457,676, ui/search/SearchScreen.kt:1060, ui/favorites/FavoritesScreen.kt:551,625, ui/listing/ListingPriceHistory.kt:70,76,97). formatPriceAmount() also hard-codes whole-unit thresholds — `price >= 1_000_000` renders '1.00M' meaning one million currency units, not one million cents.

Impact: any future caller (or iOS port) that trusts the 'minor units / cents' docstring and passes cents will render prices 100x too large AND cross the M/K abbreviation thresholds 100x early. This is a latent money-formatting contract defect, not a style nit. Landable mobile-only fix: correct the KDoc to 'whole-currency units (sub-unit scale already dropped by DecimalAsLongSerializer)', matching the serializer's own wording.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoInitiation.kt:buildUrl — `fun buildUrl(state: String): String = "$PM_APP_SCHEME://sso?callback=$CALLBACK&state=$state"` splices CALLBACK (= 'reality://sso', containing ':' and '//') into a query-parameter VALUE with no percent-encoding, and does not encode `state` either.

This is the asymmetric mirror of the inbound path, which is careful: navigation/DeepLinkRouter.kt.urlDecode form-url-DEcodes every query component and its KDoc records a previously-shipped encode/decode parity bug ('The shared router previously returned the raw, still-encoded substring ... breaking SSO validation on iOS'). The outbound leg has no matching encode step.

Currently non-exploitable because CALLBACK is a fixed constant with no '&' or extra '=' and the minted `state` nonce is 64-char hex (URL-safe) — but it is brittle: the moment the callback or state carries a reserved character ('&', '=', a query of its own) the PM app's query parser will mis-split the URL. Landable mobile-only fix: percent-encode the callback and state values (e.g. Ktor `encodeURLParameter()` / `encodeURLQueryComponent()`) in buildUrl, symmetric with DeepLinkRouter's decode. Covered by the existing SsoInitiationTest surface.
